name: AI search and enterprise knowledge retrieval
summary: Search systems retrieve relevant, permissioned information and use AI to turn it into a cited answer.
useCase: An employee asks which customer commitments differ from the standard contract and gets an answer linked to approved records they can access.
whyNow: Language models make search more conversational, while retrieval systems can supply fresher, organization-specific evidence. Glean’s reported annual recurring revenue grew from US$200 million in December 2025 to US$300 million in May 2026. That is evidence of one vendor’s commercial traction, not a measurement of the entire search market or an assurance that every generated answer is correct.

mainstream.scope: Permission-aware, source-linked AI retrieval used routinely within medium and large knowledge-intensive organizations.
mainstream.rationale: Useful products exist and distribution through cloud, productivity and data platforms is strong. Broader mainstream use requires reliable connectors, document freshness and access controls. The estimate assumes organizations treat source attribution and permission correctness as product requirements, rather than relying on fluent answers alone.

metric.name: Glean annual recurring revenue — company proxy
metric.limitations: ARR is a run-rate measure, not recognized annual revenue. Company-reported thresholds are dated snapshots and combine search, assistants and agents. No whole-market adoption share or 2021–2024 annual series is inferred.
metric.futureNote: No credible like-for-like public ARR forecast is used. Expansion should be tracked through retained enterprise usage, renewal and paid-seat growth.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: No comparable enterprise AI-search adoption metric identified for this year.
No consistent annual revenue or deployment measurement supplied.
No comparable whole-market retrieval adoption count identified.
OpenAI introduced ChatGPT search, a major distribution milestone for source-linked conversational search.
ChatGPT search expanded to users without signup; Glean passed US$200 million ARR in December.
Glean reported more than US$300 million ARR in May, including broader enterprise AI functionality.

tailwinds: Organizations already have valuable internal documents, application data and search budgets.
Retrieval can improve freshness and provide traceable sources for answers.
bottlenecks: Bad access control can disclose information the user was never entitled to see.
Stale connectors, conflicting documents and misleading citations limit trust and retention.
watchMetrics: Correctly sourced answer rate and permission-leak rate on organization-specific evaluations.
Weekly retained users, query success, renewal and cost per resolved information request.
